UNH.rationale: UNH presents an extremely unattractive risk/reward at current levels. The quantitative specialist's analysis reveals a severe valuation-to-fundamentals disconnect: trailing PE has expanded to 30.1x (top of 365-day range) while net margin has halved from 5.6% to 2.8% and ROE has collapsed from 22.8% to 12.3% over the past year. Earnings yield of 3.3% sits below the 10-year Treasury yield of 4.57%, meaning investors are not compensated for equity risk. While the Q2 2026 earnings beat ($6.38 vs $4.90 consensus) and guidance raise to $19.50-$20.00 adjusted EPS represent a positive near-term catalyst, the forward PE of ~21-22x still embeds significant optimism for a company deliberately shrinking its membership base (Medicare Advantage down 965K since year-end 2025) and facing a DOJ investigation into its vertically integrated model. The MCR improvement to 86.7% included $860M of favorable prior-period development, masking underlying cost pressures. Berkshire Hathaway's complete exit of its 5M+ share position signals institutional skepticism. The stock has rallied 34.8% from its April trough on multiple expansion alone, not earnings growth, creating asymmetric downside risk if the recovery narrative falters.
